entrypoints.summary: A trace following loop-device activity reaches pathname lookup, squashfs_lookup, squashfs_read_metadata, and then squashfs_copy_data while processing Squashfs metadata.

affected_components.role: The metadata reader gains the bounds check; the crash trace identifies the copy routine as the faulting operation.

negative_controls: The patched path returns -EIO for negative offsets.
No fixed-kernel execution result is included in the supplied artifacts.
observability.positive_marker: General protection fault in squashfs_copy_data with a KASAN possible wild-memory-access indication.

preconditions: A Squashfs lookup processes filesystem metadata containing the corrupted index-table state.
The affected code lacks the later offset-range check.

trigger_steps.summary: Cause pathname lookup to enter the Squashfs metadata-reading path; the recorded trace then reaches squashfs_copy_data after squashfs_read_metadata.

impact.affected_asset: Availability and memory safety of the Linux kernel handling Squashfs metadata.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the documented kernel memory-safety crash when the malformed filesystem state is processed; no code-execution or privilege-escalation capability is established.
impact.security_effect: Kernel general protection fault / denial of service through an out-of-bounds memory access during Squashfs metadata lookup.

causal_trace.summary: A corrupted Squashfs index lookup table produces a negative metadata-block offset.
Before metadata-copy processing, the offset was not rejected when it was negative or outside the metadata-block range.
squashfs_read_metadata passes the negative offset to squashfs_copy_data, where it causes an out-of-bounds access.
The recorded execution faults in squashfs_copy_data with a KASAN-associated general protection fault and possible wild-memory access.

failure.operation: Out-of-bounds access in squashfs_copy_data after propagation of a negative metadata offset.

primary_invariant.statement: A metadata offset used by squashfs_read_metadata must be nonnegative and strictly less than SQUASHFS_METADATA_SIZE.
primary_invariant.violated_because: A corrupted index lookup table can yield a negative metadata-block offset that reached the metadata-copy path.

quality.review_notes: The issue record documents a concrete crash and says reproducer assets exist, but their bodies and malformed image contents are not included in this bundle. The source establishes a crash and an upstream fix, not exploitability beyond denial of service or the exact attacker-controlled image layout. The negative fixed-path expectation is inferred from the patch's explicit -EIO return and is not an observed test-run result.

remediation.invariant_restored: squashfs_read_metadata rejects offsets below zero and offsets greater than or equal to SQUASHFS_METADATA_SIZE before entering the metadata-copy loop.
mitigation_classes: fail closed with -EIO before metadata-copy processing

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The supplied material identifies a corrupted index lookup table but does not provide the malformed image or exact construction steps.
data_structure_invariants: Index-derived metadata offsets must remain within the metadata block range before metadata-copy processing.

state_context.state_machine: Filesystem metadata lookup processes an index-derived metadata offset through squashfs_read_metadata before cache-copy processing.

oracle.expected_negative: With the range-check patch, out-of-range metadata offsets return -EIO from squashfs_read_metadata rather than proceeding to the metadata-copy loop.
oracle.expected_positive: On the recorded crashing kernel, Squashfs lookup reaches squashfs_copy_data and produces the reported general protection fault / KASAN-associated wild-memory-access indication.
